title: Effects of elephants on seed dispersal and germination of Balanites maughamii in an East African dry coastal forest
content:
Abstract
Elephants play a significant role in shaping tropical ecosystems. They influence the dispersal and regeneration of various plant species and thus shape plant and animal communities. In this study, we investigate seed predation rates by the African elephant on the torchwood forest tree (Balanites maughamii) in a part of the Arabuko Sokoke dry coastal forest in southern Kenya. We test for effects on the germination and seedling growth rates in ex situ experiments and consider the role of passing through the elephant gut and the effect of elephant dung on germination. Seed predation rates were highest close to parent trees. Seeds that passed through elephant guts had the highest germination and growth rates. Seeds enclosed by dung did not show higher rates of germination than seeds without dung. In general, our results underline the important role of elephants for seed dispersal and germination of B. maughamii in tropical forest ecosystems.
